- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early-to-mid horizon.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; increase early forecast values, especially if recent history shows downward momentum.
- Model often overreacts to short-term sentiment spikes — if sentiment jumps to 1.00, forecast may overshoot; cap 30d forecast at 2x recent high or 1.5x recent mean if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and history shows mean-reverting trend, model tends to overpredict; apply downward bias to mid-to-late horizon.
- Model frequently fails to capture long-term mean reversion after sharp spikes — if true outcome shows >10x spike, reduce forecast for next 7–14 days by 30–50% unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1.00, 0.00, 1.00), model may misread trend; use sentiment smoothing (avg last 3 sentiment values) to adjust forecast slope.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome shows >50% deviation from 14d moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent mean, especially if sentiment is flat or mildly negative.
